title: Hacksaw Blades in Frozen Meat Freed Two Killers

narration: Frozen hamburger meat freed two killers.
The manhunt took 23 days and 1,300 officers.
shots.visual_description: dm43 tailor (cold grade); dm43_mitchell (silhouette): examine -> hand_to_face -> stand_tense -> arms_crossed; camera push/pull; overlays: label '23 DAYS · 1,300 OFFICERS'.

sources.claim_text: Joyce Mitchell, the tailor-shop supervisor at Clinton Correctional Facility, hid hacksaw blades (and other tools) inside frozen hamburger meat left in a tailor-shop refrigerator; a corrections officer carried the meat to Matt and Sweat. Narration: 'Frozen hamburger meat freed two killers'; both men were convicted murderers.

The manhunt lasted 23 days (6-28 June 2015). The number of officers rose over the search: more than 1,100 (AP), more than 1,200, and more than 1,300 on the final days (WTVR/CNN wire, ABC7 timeline). Narration: '23 days and 1,300 officers'.

narration: Dannemora, New York. So how did they do it?
shots.visual_description: mapflight (none grade); camera push/pull; overlays: label 'CLINTON CORRECTIONAL FACILITY'.

sources.claim_text: Clinton Correctional Facility is a maximum-security prison in Dannemora, New York, near the Canadian border; the escape was discovered on the morning of 6 June 2015 (the Inspector General's report title uses the night of 5 June).

narration: Prison tailor Joyce Mitchell hid hacksaw blades inside.
shots.visual_description: dm43 tailor (cold grade); dm43_mitchell (silhouette): examine -> present -> examine -> hands_together; keyed camera moves; overlays: impact, card 'THE TAILOR SHOP / JOYCE MITCHELL · SHOP SUPERVISOR / BLADES, CHISELS, A PUNCH, A BIT'.

overlays.text: THE TAILOR SHOP / JOYCE MITCHELL · SHOP SUPERVISOR / BLADES, CHISELS, A PUNCH, A BIT

sources.claim_text: Mitchell smuggled hacksaw blades, chisels, a punch and a screwdriver bit into the prison by hiding them in frozen meat she placed in a tailor-shop refrigerator; she was arrested on 12 June 2015 and pleaded guilty on 28 July 2015.

narration: A guard carried it to Matt and Sweat.
shots.visual_description: dm43 block (night grade); dm43_palmer (silhouette): walk -> present -> stand_tense (walks); dm43_matt (silhouette): stand -> examine -> present; dm43_sweat (silhouette): stand -> point; keyed camera moves; overlays: label 'A CORRECTIONS OFFICER', card 'RICHARD MATT · DAVID SWEAT / BOTH SERVING TIME FOR MURDER'.

overlays.text: RICHARD MATT · DAVID SWEAT / BOTH SERVING TIME FOR MURDER

sources.claim_text: Corrections officer Gene Palmer took the frozen hamburger meat (containing the hacksaw blade) to Sweat and Matt in a block where inmates could cook; he said he did not know of the escape plan. In February 2016 he pleaded guilty to promoting prison contraband, tampering with evidence and official misconduct and was sentenced to six months in county jail.

Richard Matt was serving 25 years to life for a 1997 kidnapping and murder; David Sweat was serving life without parole for the 2002 killing of a sheriff's deputy. The crimes are never depicted; the card names them as convicted murderers.

narration: Three warning signs. Save this post.
shots.visual_description: dm43 block (night grade); dm43_palmer (silhouette): walk -> stand (walks); keyed camera moves; overlays: lesson 'TOOLS HIDDEN IN FOOD / A GUARD DOING FAVOURS / 400 BED CHECKS SKIPPED / NY Inspector General, 2016'.

overlays.text: TOOLS HIDDEN IN FOOD / A GUARD DOING FAVOURS / 400 BED CHECKS SKIPPED / NY Inspector General, 2016

sources.claim_text: LESSON CARD (Inspector General, June 2016): tools reached the men hidden in food (frozen meat); Officer Palmer was won over with Matt's paintings and did favours in return (art supplies, catwalk access, warnings of cell searches, passing the meat); had any one of about 400 required night bed checks been done properly the scheme would have been foiled, and 15 required cell inspections were not done. Rows: 'TOOLS HIDDEN IN FOOD', 'A GUARD DOING FAVOURS', '400 BED CHECKS SKIPPED'.

narration: They cut through steel, then a steam pipe.
shots.visual_description: dm43 tunnel (warm grade); dm43_sweat (silhouette): kneel -> examine -> kneel -> examine -> kneel -> examine -> kneel -> examine -> kneel -> examine -> kneel -> examine -> kneel; dm43_matt (silhouette): torch_low -> torch_low -> stand_tense; keyed camera moves; overlays: label 'THE STEAM TUNNELS', funfact 'THEY LEFT A NOTE ON THE PIPE: / "HAVE A NICE DAY."'.

overlays.text: THEY LEFT A NOTE ON THE PIPE: / "HAVE A NICE DAY."

sources.claim_text: The two men cut through the steel at the back of their cells, worked their way through the prison's underground tunnels and cut a hole in a steam pipe to reach a sewer/manhole outside the walls; their beds were stuffed to look occupied during night checks.

FUN FACT CARD: they left a note on the cut pipe reading 'Have a nice day' (reports differ on the drawing with it: a smiley face or a caricature). The card quotes the three words only, which all sources share.

narration: June 6th: out through a manhole. Their driver never came.
shots.visual_description: dm43 street (night grade); dm43_sweat (silhouette): stand_tense -> point -> stand_tense; dm43_matt (silhouette): stand -> hand_to_face -> arms_crossed; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: label '6 JUNE 2015 · MORNING COUNT', impact, card 'THE GETAWAY DRIVER: MITCHELL / SHE NEVER CAME · THEY FLED ON FOOT'.

overlays.text: THE GETAWAY DRIVER: MITCHELL / SHE NEVER CAME · THEY FLED ON FOOT

sources.claim_text: On the night of 5-6 June 2015 the men climbed out of a manhole on a street near the prison; the empty cells were found at the morning count on 6 June 2015.

Mitchell had agreed to be the getaway driver and was to meet the men near the prison at midnight; she did not come (she went to hospital with a panic attack), so the two fled on foot. Sheriff Favro suggested she was a 'Plan B'.

narration: Mitchell was arrested. The killers? Gone.
shots.visual_description: dm43 woods (night grade); dm43_trooper: torch -> torch (walks); dm43_officer: torch_low -> torch (walks); keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: card 'JOYCE MITCHELL ARRESTED / 12 JUNE 2015 · DAY 7 OF THE HUNT', label '1,300 OFFICERS · $1M A DAY'.

overlays.text: JOYCE MITCHELL ARRESTED / 12 JUNE 2015 · DAY 7 OF THE HUNT

sources.claim_text: Mitchell was arrested and arraigned on the night of 12 June 2015 (day 7 of the manhunt) on promoting prison contraband and criminal facilitation.

The manhunt lasted 23 days (6-28 June 2015). The number of officers rose over the search: more than 1,100 (AP), more than 1,200, and more than 1,300 on the final days (WTVR/CNN wire, ABC7 timeline). Narration: '23 days and 1,300 officers'.

narration: Day 21: Border Patrol shot Richard Matt dead.
shots.visual_description: cabin woods (cold grade); dm43_agent: stand_tense -> point -> hand_to_face; dm43_officer: torch -> stand_tense -> bowed; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: label '26 JUNE 2015 · NEAR MALONE, NY', impact, card 'RICHARD MATT · SHOT DEAD / BORDER PATROL TACTICAL TEAM · DAY 21'.

overlays.text: RICHARD MATT · SHOT DEAD / BORDER PATROL TACTICAL TEAM · DAY 21

sources.claim_text: On Friday 26 June 2015 (day 21) Richard Matt was shot dead by a member of a U.S. Customs and Border Protection (Border Patrol) tactical team in woods south of Malone, NY, after officials said he did not comply with a challenge. A line and a card only; nothing is depicted.

narration: Day 23: Sweat was caught, two miles from Canada.
shots.visual_description: dm43 road (dawn grade); dm43_sweat (silhouette): walk -> stand_tense -> hands_behind (walks); dm43_trooper: stand_tense -> point -> walk -> stand; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: label '28 JUNE 2015 · CONSTABLE, NY', impact, card 'ABOUT 2 MILES FROM CANADA / DAY 23 · THE MANHUNT ENDS'.

overlays.text: ABOUT 2 MILES FROM CANADA / DAY 23 · THE MANHUNT ENDS

sources.claim_text: On Sunday 28 June 2015 (day 23) State Police Sgt. Jay Cook, alone on patrol, shot and captured David Sweat, who was unarmed and running for a tree line, near Constable, NY, about 1.5 to 2 miles from the Canadian border (NPR: about a mile and a half; others: less than two miles). The card says 'about 2 miles'; nothing is depicted beyond a silhouette being cuffed.

narration: Mitchell was out by 2020. Sweat never will be.
shots.visual_description: dm43 tailor (cold grade); dm43_mitchell (silhouette): stand -> walk -> bowed -> hands_together; camera push/pull; overlays: card 'MITCHELL: 2 1/3 TO 7 YRS · OUT 2020 · PALMER: 6 MONTHS / SWEAT: 3 1/2 TO 7 MORE YRS, ON LIFE WITHOUT PAROLE'.

overlays.text: MITCHELL: 2 1/3 TO 7 YRS · OUT 2020 · PALMER: 6 MONTHS / SWEAT: 3 1/2 TO 7 MORE YRS, ON LIFE WITHOUT PAROLE

sources.claim_text: Mitchell was sentenced on 28 September 2015 to 2 1/3 to 7 years (promoting prison contraband, with a concurrent one year for criminal facilitation) and was released from Bedford Hills to community supervision in early February 2020. Palmer: six months (2016). Sweat: on 3 February 2016, 3 1/2 to 7 more years for the escape plus restitution of $79,841.
Sweat was already serving life without the possibility of parole for the 2002 murder of a sheriff's deputy, so the added years change nothing about release. Narration: 'Sweat never will be' (out).

Narration: 'Frozen hamburger meat freed two killers'; both men were convicted murderers.
